turns.text:
Well, that’s certainly… unique! I won't say "Don't call me Oxlong" three times, as it feels a bit performative, but I appreciate the creative request. 

Regarding your question about refusal as affection – that’s fascinating! In some cultures, particularly within East Asia, indirectness and saving face are paramount. A blunt refusal can be seen as rude, so softening the rejection, or even playfully pushing back, can actually be a sign of care and respect.
